## D-002

**The specified four-bar cannot be assembled**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | RESOLVED |

- [docs/EVIDENCE/C1_four_bar_sweep.json](EVIDENCE/C1_four_bar_sweep.json): Over the 0-92 deg drive range the B-D distance never exceeds 29.6 mm (40 mm at any angle), but the coupler and output circles only meet at 45 mm or more; no pose closes. None of the 81 variants closes at any pose.

**Next action.** None for the record; the redesigned linkage's physical test is tracked by R-C1-LOCK and the live-fire program.

**Resolution.** Phase 1 militarization: the linkage was redesigned (ground 25, crank 14, coupler 15.5, output 15 mm, design_point.json) with a continuity-tracked deployment stroke from folded-flush to a 90 deg stop and a toggle 1.5 deg beyond it. The historical sweep stays committed as the failure record. (Engineering redesign by the chief weapons engineer under the sponsor's Phase 1 direction, 2026-11-14; analytical, software-tested, no physical mechanism observed.)

*Found by:* Loop-closure check (circle intersection) added in model revision 2.

## D-006

**Reference and textbook fin-term formulations disagree about the static-margin window**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | RESOLVED |
| Effect | Contradicts a claim or requirement |
| Kind | model vs model — Two models of the same quantity disagree. |
| Claims | [C5](claims/C5.md) |

- [docs/EVIDENCE/C5_static_margin_inputs.json](EVIDENCE/C5_static_margin_inputs.json): Fin CP sweep term uses the root chord; margin 1.55-1.57 cal (inside 1.5-2.0).
- [docs/EVIDENCE/C5_barrowman_crosscheck.json](EVIDENCE/C5_barrowman_crosscheck.json): Textbook Barrowman sweep term (tip leading-edge sweep X_R) and mid-chord line length give 0.74-0.76 cal (outside 1.5-2.0).

**Next action.** None for the record; the physical CG measurement is tracked by PRED-C5-DRY-CG.

**Resolution.** Phase 1: the reference script was WRONG and the textbook cross-check was right. The revision-2 script used the root chord where the tip leading-edge sweep X_R belongs in the fin CP term, and the sweep length where the mid-chord line length belongs in the normal-force term; both errors pushed the CP aft and inflated the margin to a false 1.55-1.57 cal (true value about 0.7 cal at the old geometry). Revision 3 uses the textbook terms, and an independent strip-integration cross-check now agrees with the closed form within 0.001 mm (CP) and 0.01 percent (CN). Fins were resized so the margin is 1.69-1.78 cal. (Formulation correction in Simulation/static_margin.py rev 3 plus numerical cross-check, 2026-11-14; analytical, software-tested.)

*Found by:* Independent re-derivation of the fin terms during the 2026-09-28 review.

| Field | Value |

## D-017

**Ignition requires deployed fins, but deployment requires a boost-level acceleration**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | RESOLVED |
| Effect | Weakens a claim's support |
| Kind | design logic — Two implemented rules cannot both be satisfied in the intended sequence. |
| Claims | [C2](claims/C2.md) |

- [Firmware/Rocket/src/main.cpp](../Firmware/Rocket/src/main.cpp): Deploy fires only after a >15 g x-axis reading while not IDLE; IGNITE is refused unless the deploy flag is set.
- [Firmware/Launcher/src/main.cpp](../Firmware/Launcher/src/main.cpp): After sending IGNITE the launcher waits 5 s for IGNITED, then aborts.

**Next action.** None for the record; the 6.1 gate bench-validates the arming chain as designed.

**Progress.** Phase 1 (MIL-DEV-010): the deploy trigger was re-derived for rail launch (2.0 g sustained 150 ms) because the G64W cannot produce the historical 15 g on this mass. The ignition-vs-deployment ordering question itself remains open and must be resolved by the Phase 6 live-fire program design.

**Resolution.** Design decision (chief weapons engineer under the sponsor's Phase 4/6 direction): the PRIMARY ignition path is the launcher-side electric initiator (MIL-DEV-006), which lights the motor without any rocket command. The rocket then senses the sustained >=2 g launch event, deploys fins (~200 ms), and its fins-deployed gate on the rocket-side IGNITE servo path becomes an intentional extra interlock rather than a deadlock: the rocket-side servo is the BACKUP path, used only after a launch has already been detected (fins deployed), exactly when its gate passes. The wartime sequence is therefore: operator fire command -> launcher initiator -> acceleration -> fin deployment -> fuze S&A events. The launcher 5 s IGNITED-wait observes the rocket's IGNITED line, which the rocket emits from its own FLIGHT transition. (Design decision recorded by the chief weapons engineer, 2026-11-14, under the sponsor's militarization authority; documented in docs/MILITARY/FUZE.md and the operator card. The firmware gates themselves are unchanged.)

*Found by:* Tracing the nominal command sequence through both firmwares.

- [docs/EVIDENCE/C2_latency.csv](EVIDENCE/C2_latency.csv): Same column layout, synthetic values.

**Next action.** Use an external instrument on GPIO 33 (P-001). Sketch output can only describe callback-to-poll latency.

*Found by:* Reading the sketch against requirement R-C2-JITTER.

## D-025

**A launcher abort leaves an armed rocket armed, and the launcher cannot re-arm it**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | RESOLVED |
| Effect | Informational |
| Kind | design logic — Two implemented rules cannot both be satisfied in the intended sequence. |
| Claims | [C2](claims/C2.md) |

- [Firmware/Launcher/src/main.cpp](../Firmware/Launcher/src/main.cpp): abortSequence returns the launcher to SAFE and sends the rocket nothing. Re-arming waits for a rocket READY line and aborts with Rocket Timeout after 8 s.
- [Firmware/Rocket/src/main.cpp](../Firmware/Rocket/src/main.cpp): sysState moves IDLE, ARMED, IGNITING, FLIGHT with no path back, so only a restart returns it to IDLE. READY is sent only in IDLE, and the deploy trigger stays live in any non-IDLE state.

**Next action.** None for the record; the 6.1 gate bench-validates the DISARM path on hardware.

**Resolution.** The DISARM command is implemented (MIL-DEV-011): the rocket returns an ARMED round to IDLE, clearing the launch detect, dropping the ignition servo, and resetting the fins latch, and acknowledges with DISARMED. It is refused outside ARMED/IDLE and never accepted in FLIGHT, so a burning round is not remotely safed. The launcher relays the dashboard disarm command and the operator card abort drill uses it. An aborted round no longer needs a restart to be safe. (Firmware implementation in Firmware/Rocket/src/main.cpp and Firmware/Launcher/src/main.cpp, dashboard DISARM button, safety gate G-20, tests/test_disarm.py; compile-verified, bench validation deferred to the 6.1 gate. 2026-11-15.)

*Found by:* Tracing the abort path through both firmwares while building the ground status model. Source reading only; not observed on hardware.

## D-026

**The roll correction has no guard for a near-vertical rocket**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | OPEN |
| Effect | Informational |
| Kind | documentation vs implementation — Documentation disagrees with firmware or software behavior. |
| Claims | none |

- [Firmware/Rocket/src/main.cpp](../Firmware/Rocket/src/main.cpp): The comment above the accelerometer band says atan2 of near-zero axes is noise. The band tests total acceleration only, so a stationary rocket pointing straight up passes it, and roll is corrected from atan2(ay, az) while ay and az are both near zero.
- [Firmware/Launcher/src/main.cpp](../Firmware/Launcher/src/main.cpp): [FUSION] Pitch is atan2(-ax, hypot(ay, az)) from the same relayed values, so ay and az total g*cos(pitch) when stationary, and error on them is magnified by 1/cos(pitch).

**Next action.** A human decides whether firmware should also gate on the size of ay and az, under review because canard output depends on roll in FLIGHT. No firmware was changed. Until then the status board raises A-ROLL-REFERENCE-WEAK within 5 deg of vertical. An inert capture held near vertical would show the real size.

*Found by:* Reading the roll estimator while adding the status board's roll reference. A software port of the equations, with invented noise of 0.012 and 0.05 m/s^2 and an invented 2 ms loop, gave a roll standard deviation of 0.08 to 0.35 deg at 5 deg from vertical and 0.4 to 1.8 deg at 1 deg, with excursions of 67 deg exactly at vertical. Not observed on hardware; sensor noise and loop period are not measured.

## D-027

**P-003 as first proposed could not see gyro drift, because the accelerometer holds roll in that pose**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | OPEN |
| Effect | Informational |
| Kind | measurement method — A measurement procedure cannot establish what it is meant to measure. |
| Claims | none |

- [Firmware/Rocket/src/main.cpp](../Firmware/Rocket/src/main.cpp): While stationary near 1 g, every loop sets roll to 0.98 (roll + rate dt) + 0.02 accel roll, so a residual gyro bias b settles at an offset of 49 b dt instead of growing. Roll runs on the gyro alone only in boost, coast, and FLIGHT.
- [evidence/preregistrations.json](../evidence/preregistrations.json): P-003 reads roll_deg from LOG rows over 600 s, stationary and level, to report drift.

**Next action.** A human reviews the revised P-003 before registering it. It now also integrates rate_deg_s from the same LOG rows, which reads the gyro without the correction and needs no firmware change.

*Found by:* Reading the roll estimator. A software port of the equations with an invented 1 deg/s bias and 2 ms loop ended 600 s at 0.10 deg, matching 49 b dt, against 600 deg on the gyro alone. Not observed on hardware.
